title: Edge VPC risk-assisted approval checklist and audit playbook (WIP)
body:
Purpose:
This is a working playbook for an operator-facing approval flow that combines automated risk scoring with human checkpoints for customer-managed VPC/edge onboarding and change approvals. Goal is to reduce manual review time while preserving forensic auditability for compliance reviews.

Scope (what this doc covers):
- New customer edge/VPC onboarding and initial connectivity provisioning
- Non-breaking network config changes (route/table adjustments, peering metadata, ACL updates)
- Emergency rollbacks and post-approval audits
- Audit log shape, retention tiers, and evidence bundles for handoff to security/compliance teams

Out of scope:
- Full on-prem appliance installation guides (separate runbook)
- Low-level cryptographic KMS details (KMS team owns)

High-level idea: Risk-Assisted Approval
- Every change request submitted through the private-deploy console generates a structured Change Request (CR) object.
- An automated risk-scoring service evaluates the CR against historical telemetry, customer profile, and heuristics (e.g., exposure changes, CIDR overlap, operator identity reputation, prior rollback frequency).
- Score buckets: low (auto-approve), medium (operator review with recommended checks), high (block until additional attestation).
- All decisions emit an immutable evidence bundle (signed event + snapshot of related audit logs) stored in the customer-specific audit ledger.

Actors & responsibilities:
- Customer Network Owner: creates CR, supplies attestation when requested.
- Redwood Edge Operator: reviews medium/high CRs, can accept/deny, escalate to security.
- Automated Risk Service: returns risk_score and suggested audit level.
- Audit Collector: collects flow logs, BGP session metrics, TLS handshake metadata (if applicable), and stores in retention tier.

User stories (examples):
1) As a customer network owner, I open a CR to add a new peering route. The automated risk service returns low risk and the CR is auto-approved. I receive a signed approval receipt.
2) As an operator, I receive a medium-risk CR with recommended checklist: verify CIDR != existing corp ranges, confirm no admin-port exposure, confirm customer attestation provided. I can approve after checking snapshots.
3) As security reviewer, I download the evidence bundle for a high-risk change and validate the signed ledger contains the operator approval with timestamp and identity.

Acceptance criteria (MVP):
- CR schema defined and accepted by console/CLI (fields: id, customer_id, change_type, proposed_diff, initiator, attestation_refs).
- Risk service returns {score:int, bucket:string, rationale:list-of-strings} in < 800ms 95th percentile.
- Auto-approved CRs transition to applied state and emit signed receipts.
- Operator UI shows recommended checklist and links to evidence snapshot for medium/high CRs.
- Evidence bundle format defined and can be exported via API (JSON+tar.gz with logs, config diffs, signatures).

Audit log shape (important):
- Event types: CR_CREATED, RISK_EVALUATED, CR_AUTO_APPROVED, CR_OPERATOR_APPROVED, CR_REJECTED, CR_APPLIED, CR_ROLLBACK_INITIATED, CR_EVIDENCE_EXPORTED
- Common event fields (flat schema): timestamp, event_id, cr_id, actor_id, actor_role, request_id, change_summary, risk_score, decision, reason_codes, signature_ref
- Storage tiers: hot (30d fast search), warm (90d indexed), cold (1y raw archived), retrieval API with signed access logs for exports.

Evidence bundle contents (per CR):
- CR JSON snapshot at time-of-decision
- Risk service rationale text and model version
- Operator checklist annotations (if any)
- Relevant network telemetry snapshot (flow logs sample, peer states) pinned to the time window
- Signed operator approval receipt (identity metadata + signature)
- Export manifest with checksums and retrieval metadata

Operator flow (medium/high): checklist & playbook
- Step 0: Open CR and review summary + automated rationale.
- Step 1: Check CIDR/ACL diffs against customer baseline (link opens diff viewer).
- Step 2: Validate that no external exposure flags are raised (e.g., internet-facing admin ports).
- Step 3: Confirm customer attestation (if required). If attestation missing, request customer to add via console chat or email.
- Step 4: Approve or Reject. If Approve, include justification note. If Reject, mark next steps and required remediation.
- Step 5: System applies change (or schedules) and emits CR_APPLIED event + evidence bundle.

Rollback scenarios (examples):
- Auto rollback: If post-apply observability detects BGP flap > threshold or spike in 5xxs attributable to the change, system triggers CR_ROLLBACK_INITIATED and notifies operator + customer.
- Manual rollback: Operator opens a Rollback CR referencing original CR id, attaches failure logs, and approves rollback; evidence bundle created.

Telemetry & SLOs to track:
- Risk service latency (p95 target < 800ms).
- Auto-approval rate by customer segment (baseline expected 60% for established customers).
- Time-to-operator-decision for medium/high CRs (target median < 30 minutes for weekday business hours).
- Evidence export success rate and integrity check pass rate.

Security & Data retention notes:
- Evidence bundles are encrypted with customer KMS when stored in cold tier. Access control audited (who exported, when, why).
- Minimal PII in audit logs; when required, redaction policy documented and automatable.

Implementation sketch (high level):
- API: POST /crs -> validate -> write CR -> risk-service evaluate async -> event stream -> apply/queue.
- Risk-service: python microservice with feature store (customer history, operator reputation), model v1 = rules + weighted heuristics, v2 = ML scoring pipeline (3 months).
- Audit ledger: append-only store (immutable), signatures via internal signing service for platform attestations.
- UI: console pane for "Pending CRs" with risk ribbon, checklist suggestions and "evidence" link that opens snapshot viewer.

Open questions / tradeoffs:
- What counts as "attestation" from the customer? Signed API call vs. human confirmation in console? (need legal input)
- How aggressive should auto-approve be for newly onboarded customers with no history? (possible ramp: stricter for first 30 days)
- Evidence bundle retention SLAs for enterprise vs. self-serve customers (tiered pricing).
- Do we allow operator-level overrides for low-risk auto-approved CRs? Risk: undermines automation trust; Benefit: quick mitigation.

Risks & mitigations:
- False negatives (high-risk change auto-approved): mitigate by conservative initial thresholds and fast detection/rollback hooks.
- Audit gaps if telemetry sampling misses the relevant window: mitigation = pin time window and store higher-fidelity samples for medium/high CRs for a configurable retention window.

Next steps (short-term):
- Sync with Security and Legal to define acceptable customer attestation forms (owner: Priya). Due: 2025-12-10.
- Prototype risk-service basic heuristics and return shape. Owner: Luca. Spike due: 2026-01-07.
- Console mockups for operator checklist + evidence viewer. Owner: Elena. Due: 2025-12-15.
- Draft API schema and event definitions; add tests for exported evidence bundles. Owner: Maya/Carlos. Due: 2026-01-20.

Checklist (for next iteration):
- [ ] Finalize CR schema and event taxonomy
- [ ] Implement evidence bundle manifest format
- [ ] Define retention tiers and KMS controls with Security
- [ ] Add example export in Confluence with sample bundle
- [ ] Wire basic risk-service and run manual simulations with staging customers

Notes to self:
- Try to keep operator UI friction to a minimum; suggest pre-populated checklist items based on risk rationale.
- Save a sample evidence bundle (fake data) in confluence so compliance can see format.

References and provenance:
- Related PRD: Private edge approval vision (Confluence)
- Jira epic: PI-8123 (linked above)
- Prior experiments: sigma-edge-autoapprove-2024 (see gh:infra/edge-operator#278)

End of draft.

(Edited 2025-12-03: added rollout/rollback examples and evidence bundle manifest checklist)
